To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inoculation with arbuscular mycolrhizal fungi and 50% concentration of N, P, K and Ca fertilizers with AMF were the best treatments for improving the yield production of common beans plants.
AMF inoculation significantly enhanced the growth, yield and yield components of bean plants with minimized the levels NPK comparing with those of non myorhizal ones.
the inoculation with AM fungi significantly increased the growth of common bean plants with minimized the levels NPK fertilizers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of mycorrhiza on yield production of bean plants.

the application of AM fungi for increasing yield of common bean plants with minimized the concentrations of NPK fertilization and also with increasing the efficiency of nutrients uptake and improving the quality of common bean seeds.
the effects of AMF and different levels of N, P, K fertilizers on growth, yield and yield components of mycorrhized and non mycorhizal common bean plants under greenhouse conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AMF inoculation and 50 and 75 % concentrations of NPK with inoculation of AMF are the greatest than other concentrations of NPK and non mycorhizal plants.
the inoculation with AM fungus and the concentrations 75% of the NPK with AM fungus is the greatest than other concentrations and the non-mycorrhizal plants.
AMF application with 50 and 75% NPK concentration are the greater than others concentrations and non mycolrhizal plants in improving growth and yield of common bean plants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AMF can be used as biofertilizers for common bean production and can be applied in agriculture.
AMF inoculation of common bean plants with different levels of nutrients (NPK) significantly enhanced growth, yield components and some chemical contents of common bean seeds.
mycorrhizae have the ability to enhance growth, development and yield of common bean plants and this enhancement can be achieved by using the appropriate level of NPK fertilizes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the application of AMF in common bean plants with the concentrations of NPK (50% and %) can significantly improve the yield production and some nutrients in common bean plants.
the use of AM fungi can improve the growth and yield of common bean plants.
mycorrhizas have the capacity to increase the nutrient content and yield of common bean plants, especially when combined with lower concentrations of fertilizers.
